destination.name: Dubbo
destination.tagline: A Central West city best known for its open-range zoo, with a 19th-century gaol and limestone caves nearby.
destination.description: Dubbo is a city of 43,516 people (2021) in the Orana region, about 392 km north-west of Sydney. Taronga Western Plains Zoo, an open-range zoo with elephants, giraffes and a breeding program for rare black rhinos, is the district's biggest tourist draw. In town, Old Dubbo Gaol, an official gaol from 1859 to 1966, is now a museum, and the Royal Flying Doctor Service has a hands-on visitor experience at the airport. Wellington Caves, with guided tours of Cathedral Cave and Gaden Cave, is the usual day trip.
whyVisit: See giraffes at the open-range zoo
Take a guided tour of Wellington Caves

goodToKnow.title: Reach it without a car
goodToKnow.detail: A NSW TrainLink XPT runs daily from Sydney, usually arriving between 2 and 3 PM, and the zoo is a 5 km taxi or bus ride from town.

goodToKnow.title: Hire wheels at the zoo
goodToKnow.detail: The zoo is large, and bikes, electric carts and pedal boats can be hired there; a cycleway, the Tracker Riley Cycleway, also runs out from town.

goodToKnow.title: Cave tours are guided
goodToKnow.detail: Wellington Caves open to guided tours only, from 9 AM to 4:15 PM, at about $32.50 for an adult.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} give moderate temperatures for a day on foot or by bike around the large open-range zoo and for the cave tours.
